title: MEMD: project multichannel data to estimate a joint envelope mean
summary: MEMD uses many projection directions to construct a multivariate local mean. Its sifting preserves aligned mode slices across the input channels.

steps.title: Project the data
steps.text: Use Hammersley-based unit directions and locate extrema of each scalar projection.

steps.title: Construct vector envelopes
steps.text: At the projection extrema times, interpolate the original vector samples and average valid envelopes.

steps.title: Sift jointly
steps.text: Subtract the direction-averaged vector mean and repeat the multivariate stopping test.

steps.title: Extract aligned modes
steps.text: Remove the accepted multichannel IMF, continue on the vector residue, and keep the final residue.

parameters.name: n_dir (upstream trace)
parameters.effect: This bounded PySDKit demonstration uses 16 projection directions; the DeTime wrapper does not expose this as a documented public control.

parameters.name: Stopping rule (upstream trace)
parameters.effect: Uses PySDKit's default Rilling-style test with a safety cap of 50 sifts.

parameters.name: primary_period / explicit mode groups
parameters.effect: Used by DeTime after upstream extraction, independently of the projection directions.

cautions: This PySDKit backend requires at least three channels for MEMD; the example uses three aligned channels.
Projection count, envelope boundaries, and stopping rules affect the result.
Aligned IMF indexes do not establish physiological or other physical source identity.

references.title: Rehman and Mandic: Multivariate empirical mode decomposition

trace_kind: upstream numerical stages and execution trace
trace_note: Computed with PySDKit 0.5.0: its direction, extrema, and boundary helpers supply the vector envelopes; actual first-IMF sifting calls are recorded. The reduced direction count is a teaching setting, not a benchmark setting.
input_note: Deterministic synthetic teaching signal; not a benchmark.
